title: the wrong-tree guard exempts version whatever follows it, so version bump from outside a project rewrites that project's version
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 while 0113's consumer page for shell-init was checked against the code, and driven by cc at 142763d.

WHAT HAPPENS. The wrong-tree guard in bin/devbin refuses to act on a project you are not standing in, and it exempts `version` whatever follows it. So the WRITING sub-commands escape it. Driven in a fixture whose VERSION reads 1.2.3, from an unrelated directory:
- `<project>/bin/devbin fmt md` is refused, rc=4, as it should be.
- `<project>/bin/devbin version bump patch` prints `1.2.4` at rc=0, and the project's VERSION now reads 1.2.4.
`version set` and `version sync` pass the same exemption.

WHY. The case in bin/devbin reads `install | shell-init | -v | --version | version) _devbin_wrong_tree_check=no`, and `devbin -v|--version|version` likewise. The comment gives the reason for this group: "from an INSTALL these report what devbin is installed, and an install has no project for the guard to protect". That reason covers reading the identity. It does not cover set, bump and sync, which write the project's version file and every sidecar.

WHY IT MATTERS. `dvb` falls back to `$DEVBIN_SOURCE` when its walk finds no project, and hands the command to that tree's launcher. So `dvb version bump patch`, typed in a directory with no devbin project, bumps the version of whatever DEVBIN_SOURCE names -- devbin's own checkout, in the bootstrap setup shell-init's page describes. The page audit measured exactly that. The guard exists so that this cannot happen, and the exemption is wider than its own stated reason.

THE FIX: exempt `version` and `-v`/`--version` only when nothing follows them, or only for `show` and `check` -- the forms that write nothing -- and refuse the rest from outside the tree as every other writing verb is.

## Resolution

Fixed at c35c930. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. The wrong-tree guard exempts `version` only in the forms that write nothing: alone, show, check and its help. set, bump and sync are guarded like any writing verb, so from a foreign tree they exit 4 and leave the version file untouched. The exemption lists what may pass, so a writing sub-command added later is guarded by default. shell-init.md:28 changes with it.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Red at the base. Four mutants, all killed: version exempt whatever follows (the old rule), bump let through, show guarded, and --version guarded.
- REVIEW. cc: sound.
- THE SUITE. The full suite on the series as it landed -- land018 at c130b3a, whose 27 series paths are byte-identical to the landed commits: 1..1653, 1653 ok, 0 not ok, 4 skips (127, 135, 624, 626), rc 0, 12:39:28Z to 13:11:35Z. Each commit passed the gate (guards, critic, doctor) as it landed.
